mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate, indicative of accommodative monetary policy, reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a contraction in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate revenue growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below its 6-month moving average), manufacturing sector weakness is expected to reduce corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below its 6-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month signals strong labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 2.5% signals rising inflation expectations, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in both quarterly real GDP growth (GDPC1) and monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening in the broader economy and housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST declines for 3 consecutive months and GDPC1 growth rate (quarterly) is negative in the latest quarter, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) and strong job growth (PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% monthly), labor market tightness supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.02.
